articles.title: The First Big ‘Yes’ In Private Equity’s Slow March Into Law — See Also
articles.content:
私募基金收购律所大门虽未全开，但已迈出重要一步：查尔斯班克资本拟以7亿美元收购伍德·史密斯·亨宁与伯曼律师事务所，标志着私募基金在法律服务行业的首次重大突破。这一交易虽仍需监管审批，但已引发业界对法律服务商业化的深层思考。

托德·布兰奇潜在接班人也面临公积金问题：参议院将审查这位提名为副司法部长的候选人，他正是被指控管理"反武器化基金"的关键人物之一。该基金原本应已清算，但其复杂性可能成为确认听证会的障碍。

联邦法官言论再引争议：一位法官在多个媒体露面时多次发表反伊斯兰言论，包括将阿拉伯传统服饰称作"恐怖主义围巾"。司法委员会正在调查这位法官的系列言论，包括其他种族主义评论。

德州州长新举措挑战宪法：他签署行政令限制对某些州法的联邦审查权，法律专家指出这可能违反宪法最高法条款。此举被批评为对联邦制的挑战。

律师逃避听证会的特殊方式：一位律师在律师协会选举落败后突然触电受伤，导致听证会被迫取消。这一事件引发了对职业伦理和专业准则的讨论。

法律行业面临变革与挑战的关键时期：从资本市场对律所的兴趣，到司法体系中的言论争议，再到各级政府对宪法的不同解读，多个事件凸显了法律领域的深刻变化和复杂性。
articles.summary:
Private Equity’s Law Firm Takeover Isn’t Here, But It Just Got A Lot Closer: The reported $700 million Charlesbank deal for Wood Smith Henning & Berman gives PE a toehold in the industry.

Todd Blanche’s Potential Successor Has A Slush Fund Problem Too: The Senate is going to love this.

Federal Judges Say The Darnedest Things: Judicial complaint compiles judge’s media hits and there’s just a whole lot of bigotry.

Texas Says ‘No Thanks’ To The Constitution: Well, at least its Governor did.

That’s One Way To Get Out Of A Hearing: Condolences on losing the election.

articles.title: The Confirmation Speech That Doomed The SCOTUS Nominee It Was Meant To Save
articles.content:
编辑注：欢迎来到我们的每日栏目"每日趣味问答"！

1970年，内布拉斯加州的一名美国参议员通过广播为一位被批评者认为"学术成就平平"的最高法院提名人辩护。这位参议员的策略是承认这一点——他坚称即使提名人才能一般，普通人也应该在法院中获得一定代表权。

提示：这位提名人几周后失败，而这位参议员的"辩护"被认为是确认历史上最著名的自毁长城之一。
答案见下一页。

原文《拯救大法官提名的确认演讲最终毁了他》首发于法律之上网站。
articles.summary:
Ed. Note: Welcome to our daily feature Trivia Question of the Day!

A U.S. Senator from Nebraska took to the airwaves in 1970 to defend which Supreme Court nominee that critics had branded intellectually undistinguished? The strategy, such as it was, was to concede the point — insisting that even if the nominee were mediocre, mediocre people deserved a little representation on the Court too.

Hint: The nominee went down to defeat weeks later, and the senator’s “defense” is remembered as one of the great self-inflicted wounds in confirmation history.
See the answer on the next page.

articles.title: Neuroscience For Lawyers, A Texas Two-Step, And Rinse And Repeat In DC
articles.content:
法律院校应该教授神经科学基础吗？为什么不呢？或者作为律师继续教育（CLE）必修课呢？律所工作大多需要判断力，懂得察言观色，探究客户需求，并帮助他人解决问题，这样的课程有什么不良影响呢？也许会被视为“轻松及格”的课程，或者在不同法学院获得其他等级的成绩，可能会让那些更关注班级排名的学生望而却步。我认为了解决策过程的一点知识总是有价值的。这种知识在面试和获得至关重要的第一份工作时也不会有害。

同样，任何律师都受益于参加关于该主题的CLE课程。有些律师甚至不知道如何拼写“团结一致”，更不用说如何表现出这种行为了。这有助于增强网络互动的自信心，获得并保留客户，并为客户争取最佳结果。客户出于多种原因可能不愿向其律师完全坦白。让客户感到舒适，敢于“坦诚相告”，即所谓“没有意外”，是律师制定适合特定案件的策略的关键。这还有另一个重要功能：客户可以将问题转移到律师身上。这才是问题应该负担的地方，这样客户就可以回归自己的事业，无论是什么。

每当我认为自己对人工智能有了一点了解时，我都会惊讶于另一个人工智能的“意外”。这次不是关于幻觉的问题。对于一些全新且完全不同的事情：如何看待专家证人使用人工智能撰写其报告，并且正如预期那样，该报告为支付其费用的客户脱罪？好笑吗？不好笑。原告方的律师进行了一些调查，发现专家使用ChatGPT时的其中一个提示得出了专家想要的并为此付出了高额费用的结论。请从时间表中抽出几分钟观看链接中的陈述摘录。看到成年男人（也许假设了不在证据中的事实）像小男孩一样表现，真是令人捧腹。当然，这发生在德克萨斯州。不用说太多了。

因此，我们新任的司法部长托德·布兰奇拒绝声明司法部独立于47，这让人意外吗？在50-49的确认投票中，膝盖仍然表示对47的崇拜，尽管票数接近。令人难以置信的是（实际上并不令人难以置信），我们国家最高的执法官员（抱歉，卡什·帕特尔）认为47对是否起诉的意见与任何人的观点一样重要。难道应该就起诉问题进行调查吗？谁应该被起诉？

布兰奇说47永远不会要求他做任何跨越“伦理或道德”界限的事情，也不会逼迫他做违法或不道德的事情。布兰奇坚称这从未发生过，也不会发生。请准备好“认真脸”论点。难道不是政府的责任在有证据证明其案件超出合理怀疑的情况下才提起诉讼吗？政府对詹姆斯·科米的案件在哪里？

美国华盛顿特区检察官吉恩·皮罗有足够的判断力，因为证据不足无法支持有罪判决，所以撤销了对反映池被污染的指控。

地铁三明治案件的无罪判决呢？

与此同时，在加利福尼亚中央区，也就是所谓的“业余时间”，联邦检察官在移民抗议者的案件中连续失败。

如果布兰奇担任司法部长，而不是帕姆·邦迪，这些案件会被提起吗？你认为布兰奇会反对47的一些坚持惩罚其认为的敌人的要求吗？证据在哪里，那个证明案件所需的小东西？有人会告诉47他不能总是得逞吗，无论他有多少总统发脾气？47使用罗伊·科恩的游戏规则，这并不美观。

吉尔·斯威策已经是加利福尼亚律师协会的40多年的活跃成员了。她记得在一个更温和的时代执业。她有着多样化的法律事业，包括担任副检察官、独自执业，以及几个高级内部职位。她现在全职从事调解工作，这给了她机会观察恐龙、千禧一代和介于两者之间的人互动——并不总是文明的。你可以通过电子邮件oldladylawyer@gmail.com与她联系。
articles.summary:
Would it make sense for law schools to teach the basics of neuroscience? Why not? Or a required course for lawyers to satisfy the CLE competency requirement? Since much of what lawyers do in lawyering is judgment, ability to read the room, suss out the client’s needs, and being able to help people solve their problems, is there any downside to such a course? It might be construed as an “easy A,” or whatever grade is given in various law schools, and it might deter students who are more concerned about class rank, etc. I think there’s value in knowing at least a little about the decision-making process. That knowledge couldn’t hurt in interviews and landing that all-important first job. 

Similarly, it wouldn’t hurt any lawyer to have a CLE course on the topic. Some lawyers don’t know how to spell collegial, let alone act that way. It could help confidence in networking, getting and keeping clients, and getting the best possible result for that client. Clients can be reluctant to be completely candid with their counsel for many reasons. Making the client feel comfortable to “spill their guts,” aka “no surprises,” is essential for the lawyer to craft the strategy that makes sense in the particular case. And it has another important function: the client can offload the problem(s) to the lawyer. That’s where the burden properly belongs, so that the client can get back to business, whatever it may be. 

Every time I think I have even a little understanding about AI, I am astonished by another AI “whoops.” This one is not about hallucinations. For something new and completely different: how about an expert witness who uses AI to write his report and, of course, that report exonerates the client who had paid for it? Funny? Not funny. Plaintiff’s counsel did some sleuthing and found out that one of the prompts the expert used with ChatGPT came to the conclusion that the expert wanted and had been paid handsomely for. Spare a few minutes from time sheets and watch the deposition excerpt in the link. Hilarious to see grown men (perhaps assuming facts not in evidence) act like little boys. Of course this was in Texas. Enough said.

So, is anyone surprised that our brand new Attorney General Todd Blanche has refused to declare the Justice Department’s independence from 47? In the 50-49 confirmation vote, the knees were still bent in adulation to 47, although it was close. What’s remarkable (no, not really) is that the highest law enforcement official in our land (sorry, Kash Patel) thinks that 47’s opinion about whether to prosecute is every bit as important as anyone else’s point of view. Should surveys be taken about whether to prosecute and whom?

 Blanche said that 47 would never ask him to do something that would cross either an “ethical or moral” line, nor would 47 push him to do something illegal or unethical. Blanche insisted that hasn’t happened and will not happen. Cue the “straight face” argument. Isn’t it the government’s responsibility to file cases only if there’s evidence that can prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt? Whither the government’s case against James Comey? 

U.S. Attorney for D.C. Jeanine Pirro had the good sense to drop the case against the purported tainter of the reflecting pool since there was insufficient evidence to support a guilty verdict.  

What about the Subway sandwich case acquittal?

Meanwhile here in LaLa land, aka the Central District of California, in what some have called “Amateur Hour,” federal prosecutors have lost every case brought by the U.S. Attorney’s Office against immigration protesters.  

If Blanche had been the AG, rather than Pam Bondi, would these cases have been brought? What do you think? Will Blanche push back against some of 47’s insistence to punish his perceived enemies? Where’s the evidence, that pesky little thing needed to prove a case? Is anyone going to tell 47 that he doesn’t always get his way, no matter how many presidential tantrums? 47 uses the Roy Cohn playbook and it’s not a pretty one.

Jill Switzer has been an active member of the State Bar of California for over 40 years. She remembers practicing law in a kinder, gentler time. She’s had a diverse legal career, including stints as a deputy district attorney, a solo practice, and several senior in-house gigs. She now mediates full-time, which gives her the opportunity to see dinosaurs, millennials, and those in-between interact — it’s not always civil. You can reach her by email at oldladylawyer@gmail.com.

The post Neuroscience For Lawyers, A Texas Two-Step, And Rinse And Repeat In DC appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: Law Practice Management Company Smokeball Unveils New Global Brand Built Around ‘Powering People-Law’
articles.content:
你知道吗？法律事务管理公司Smokeball的名字来源于著名的法院案件《Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.》，该案例昭示企业必须履行其承诺的义务。因此，Smokeball今天推出的新全球品牌不仅强调了其对律师客户的赋能责任，也强调了律师对其个人客户的服务责任。

新口号是“赋能人性法律”，Smokeball表示：“减少行政事务，多为最需要您的人服务。”

在众多法律科技公司聚焦于服务大型企业的大型律所时，Smokeball有意将目标锁定在为个人服务的独资、小型或中型律师事务所的律师身上。实际上，该公司将“人性法律（“people-law”）”作为其新品牌战略的核心，并声称首创这一术语，以命名律师每日所从事的极具人文关怀的工作。

公司的新闻稿称：“新的全球品牌将人置于故事中心，反映了法律工作如何将社区凝聚在一起，而Smokeball的存在就是为了赋能这一过程。无论是面临变化的家庭、首次购房者、小企业主，还是追求正义的个人。”

Smokeball首席运营官兼联合创始人Jane Oxley在本周接受采访时表示，这不是公司在开拓新市场，而是进一步深耕现有客户群体。她指出，公司的客户律师事务所中没有一家员工超过100人，这些律师主要从事家庭法、人身伤害、房地产、刑事辩护和劳工法律等领域的法律实务。

“我们经常谈论社区，对此我们深感自豪，因为这些律师每天都在为社区服务，从事那些将我们紧密联系在一起的工作。”Oxley补充道。

Oxley表示，这一新举措是品牌更新而非重新塑造，部分目的是为了给这些律师的工作冠以一个名字——不提名字，就无法得到认可。她说：“他们知道自己所做的工作很重要，但很少有人感谢他们，反而经常抱怨他们。这项工作往往得不到回报。”

这个品牌更新源于与Smokeball美国、澳大利亚和英国的至少50位客户的交流。Oxley表示，这些交流不再关注软件，而是探讨这些律师从事这份工作的原因。

在这个过程中，公司与品牌专家合作，制定了新的愿景宣言：“我们将律师与职业自豪感联系起来”，以及新的使命宣言：“我们通过提高生产力来减轻行政负担”。

尽管使命宣言是新的，但对生产力的关注并非如此。Oxley指出，Smokeball在2012年成立后首次参加ABA TECHSHOW展览时，甚至没有计费模块。

她说：“我们从生产力开始，可能当时我们的理念有点超前。当时人们会说‘我们只需要一个计费系统’，而我们则告诉他们‘不，您需要提高效率’。”

飘扬“人性法律”的旗帜

新品牌中最显著的变化是标志。取代了长期标识Smokeball品牌的球体，新标志采用了一面旗帜，被描述为“普遍的代言人象征”。

当被问及旗帜是否象征飘扬“人性法律”的旗帜时，Oxley表示正是如此。

“确实如此，是飘扬‘人性法律’的旗帜。我们的客户是为其客户代言的美好律师，而我们则希望成为为客户代言的最佳代表。”她说。

Oxley补充道，观察仔细会发现，旗帜的直边向平等符号致敬，而标志的波纹形态则赋予其动感。

新标志更加现代化，设计旨在与主流科技公司的标识并驾齐驱。她说：“这体现了Smokeball未来几年的发展愿景。”

对于Oxley而言，公司品牌更新的两个不变因素是其名称和独特的橙色配色方案。虽然橙色保留了下来，但它现在拥有了自己的名称，叫作“力量橙”。

为什么是现在？

当被问及为什么现在进行品牌更新时，Oxley给出了两个原因。首先，Smokeball的增长速度比以往任何时候都快，在美国和澳大利亚市场份额不断扩大，并在英国建立了自己的市场。

此外，她表示，公司认为其品牌形象已落后于其技术发展，尤其是近年来由人工智能驱动的技术变革。

她说：“我们已经到了一个点，认为自己在市场中没有独特的定位，需要做得更好。展示我们在这些法律实务领域是一个强大的选择，这是我们之前没有做好的事情。”

在公司的新闻稿中，联合创始人兼首席执行官Hunter Steele重申了这一观点：“随着我们发展成为一家全球企业，我们意识到品牌形象没有跟上我们所提供的价值。这不是对Smokeball的重新发明，而是我们一直以来的本真。法律始终是、也将继续是人与人之间的事务。我们的角色是赋能从事这项工作的律师，让他们有更多时间专注于最需要他们的人。”

核心观点

简单的谷歌搜索可以确认，Smokeball并非首创“人性法律”这一术语，但其使用带连字符的人性法律（“people-law”）使其具有独特性。

尽管如此，我仍然倾向于“赋能人性法律”的定位。法律科技供应商和客户过于关注技术和创新——关注那些闪亮的物品——以至于可能会忽略法律工作的本质——律师最初为什么选择攻读法律，以及他们为谁服务。

“赋能人性法律”关注的是律师为什么从事这项工作，而不仅仅是他们使用的工具。

新品牌战略的一个简洁语句总结得恰如其分：“因为您上法学院不是为了行政事务。”

articles.title: How To Get Your Nonfiction Book Published
articles.content:
从最关键的问题开始
许多律师告诉我他们想写一本书。但真正写成的人很少，而能在开始前停下来思考最重要问题的人就更少了：我为什么想写这本书？

如果答案是为了赚钱，我建议重新考虑。确实有些作者通过写书赚到了钱，有些人甚至靠一本书开创了职业生涯。但对于大多数非小说类作者，特别是在专业领域写作的人来说，书的销售收入通常无法弥补写作、编辑、出版和推广一本书所需的数百小时。从时间回报来看，这笔账可能让人沮丧。

这并不意味着你不应该写书。而是要理解自己真正期待的回报。也许你有有益之言要表达。也许你花了20年学到的经验能帮别人省去10年。也许你想在某个领域树立自己的地位、培养年轻专业人士、建立可信度、开拓演讲机会，或将你的想法以比社交媒体更持久的形式呈现出来。这些都是写书的好理由。

书本身可能不是商业产品。它可能是你的名片、资质证明、话题引子或贡献。

**在动笔之前，先了解你的平台**
在非小说类出版领域，你会经常听到"平台"这个词。你的平台指的是你现有的接触潜在读者的能力。这不仅限于社交媒体粉丝数。它还包括LinkedIn受众、通讯订阅者、播客听众、演讲活动、协会领导职位、客户、专业网络、媒体露面、之前的出版物、课程或在特定行业的认可地位。

出版社关心平台，因为他们要做商业赌注。优秀的手稿有帮助，但出版社也想知道谁会买这本书，以及读者如何得知这本书。如果你每年在会议上为5000人演讲，有3万名高度参与的粉丝，定期在受尊重的媒体发表文章，或领导一个组织，其成员是你这本书的天然受众，那么你降低了出版社的风险。

没有魔法的粉丝数量。1万名真正关心你主题的读者，可能比10万名因其他原因关注你的人更有价值。参与度、可信度、接触性和匹配度才是关键。真正的问题不是"我需要多少粉丝？"，而是"我能否找到一群了解我、信任我，并且有理由关心这本书的受众？"

如果你的平台较小，在书出版前就开始构建它。写文章、演讲、分享有用资料、参加播客、创办通讯、参与为你的目标读者服务的组织。这样做是因为你有贡献可做，而非为了未来的销售渠道收集人头。真正的平台建立在信任之上。

**传统出版：你真正选择的东西**
传统出版通常意味着出版社购买你的书，支付出版费用，并负责编辑、设计、制作、发行和至少部分营销。具体协议可能包含预付金和超出预付金后的版税。

显而易见的优势在于可信度、专业基础设施、更广的发行范围，以及能将手稿变成成品书的团队。知名出版社能更容易让书进入书店、获得媒体关注，并进入个人作者难以触及的渠道。

代价是控制权、速度和经济效益。传统出版速度缓慢。你可能对书的标题、封面、长度、发布日期、定价，甚至内容本身的控制权较少。出版商掌握商业流程。每本书你获取的版税通常比自出版更少。

获取传统出版合约也不仅仅是完成手稿并邮件给出版社。对于许多非小说类项目，第一步实际上是书的提案。

**文学经纪人和书的提案**
许多大出版社不接受未经邀请的投稿。他们希望文学经纪人推荐项目。经纪人了解哪些编辑正在购买哪类书籍，如何定位项目，如何谈判出版协议，以及如何保护作者利益。

对于非小说类书籍，你通常是通过提案而不是完整的手稿来接触经纪人。一个有力的提案通常包括书的理念、读者群、书的现时意义、为什么你是最佳作者、竞争或类似书籍、你的平台、你的营销范围、章节大纲和样章。

这个提案迫使你回答一些必须回答的问题。这本书为谁而写？它解决什么问题？读者为什么会买这本书而不是其他50本涉及同一主题的书？你的独特观点是什么？读者如何找到你？

寻找经纪人需要调研。查找代表你类别非小说类书籍的经纪人。查看与你类似的书，看看谁是作者的经纪人。阅读代理机构的投稿指南并遵循。给数百个经纪人发送通用邮件很容易，也很容易被忽视。一次深思熟虑的查询，展示你了解经纪人的书单，虽然更费力，但出版界从未有过不努力就能获得竞争优势的时候。

拒绝是过程中的一部分。拒绝不一定意味着书写得不好。可能是时机不对，类别拥挤，平台不够大，经纪人不知道合适的编辑，或项目不符合经纪人的书单。

**自出版就是出版——但你成了出版商**
自出版已经发生了巨大变化。现在你可以专业出版一本书，销售印刷版和电子版，并触及全球读者，而无需说服传统出版社购买你的项目。

优势显著。你掌控内容、标题、封面、价格、时间表、更新和营销。你可以更快地推进。你每本书的经济效益可能更好。如果你的书服务于一个你熟悉的专业细分领域，自出版可能更合理。

但"自出版"不应意味着"我全都自己做"。传统出版社雇佣编辑、校对员、校样人员、设计师、制作专家和营销人员是有原因的。如果你自出版，你要负责组建这些团队。雇佣优秀的编辑。让人校对最终文本。投资专业封面。让书的内部看起来像一本真正的书。读者不应从成品的质量看出你的出版模式。

自出版最大的风险是没有人会告诉你书还没准备好。自由很有用，摩擦也很有用。建立自己的质量控制流程。

**选择哪条路？**
目标应决定选择。如果你的梦想是全国书店发行、主流媒体报道，以及获得知名出版社的认可和支持，寻求经纪人并追求传统出版可能值得耗费时间和承受拒绝。

如果你的目标是让高度专业化的书落入客户、同事、会议参与者、学生或专业成员手中，自出版可能更快、更合理。如果你已有直接接触最可能阅读这本书的人的渠道，你可能不需要一家出版社来建造一座你已拥有的桥梁。

独立和混合出版商也占据了两种模式之间的领域。安排各不相同。一些提供有价值的编辑和制作服务。另一些本质上是昂贵的服务包，包裹在传统出版的语言里。阅读协议。理解谁付钱给谁、谁拥有权利、实际包括哪些服务、发行如何运作，以及如果你想要回权利会发生什么。

不要因为某种模式在鸡尾酒会上听起来更威风而选择它。选择最能服务于书和你写书原因的模式。

**只写你能写的书**
市场不需要另一本任何人都能写的通用书籍。你的优势在于你的经验、观点、故事、错误、观察和你通过工作得出的结论。

这并不意味着书必须以你为主。通常不应该。读者应该是中心。你的经验只有在帮助读者理解、避免、完成或从不同角度看待某事时才有价值。

在写6万字之前，你应该能用几句话解释这本书。确定读者、读者的需求或欲望，以及读者读完这本书后会有什么不同。然后围绕这个承诺构建章节。

然后完成它。出版界充斥着"正在写一本书"的人。在某个时刻，你必须停止谈论成为作者，坐下来足够长时间、足够频繁地真正成为一位作者。

**书只是开始，不是结束**
无论你采用传统出版还是自出版，你可能都要推广这本书。出版社可以帮忙，但作者不应认为出版合约附带无限的营销机器。你可能仍然需要写文章、参加播客、在会议上演讲、在线发帖、联系组织，并向最可能从中受益的社区介绍这本书。

这也是为什么你的动机很重要。如果你写这本书是因为你关心这个主题，推广就更像是继续那场让你写这本书的对话，而非让陌生人购买某物的请求。

书可以比你走得更远。它可以触及你永远不会遇见的人。它可以在书架上放置多年，并在有人需要时恰好变得有用。它可以建立一个想法，保存你所学，并创造你在写第一页时无法预见的机会。

我们中很少有人能通过写非小说类书籍致富。这没关系。金钱只是回报的一种衡量标准。如果你有值得说的话，知道你想对谁说，并且愿意付出努力说得好，出版一本书仍然是你从事的最有价值的专业项目之一。

弗兰克·拉莫斯是迈阿密戈德堡·塞加拉的合伙人，他从事商业诉讼、产品责任和灾难性人身伤害案件。你可以在LinkedIn上关注他，他拥有约8万名粉丝。

本文最初发表于《法律之上》。

Start With the Question That Matters Most

Many lawyers tell me they want to write a book. Fewer actually write one. Fewer still stop before they begin and ask the question that probably matters most: Why do I want to do this?

If the answer is money, I would reconsider. Some authors make real money from books. Some authors turn one book into a career. But most nonfiction authors, particularly professionals writing in a niche, are not going to make enough from book sales to justify the hundreds of hours it takes to write, edit, publish, and promote a book. If you calculate your return by the hour, the math may be depressing.

That doesn’t mean you shouldn’t write one. It means you should understand the return you are actually seeking. Maybe you have something useful to say. Maybe you have spent 20 years learning lessons that could save someone else 10 years. Maybe you want to establish yourself in a field, teach younger professionals, build credibility, open doors to speaking opportunities, or put your ideas into a form that lasts longer than a social media post. Those are all good reasons to write a book.

The book itself may not be the business. It may be a calling card, a credential, a conversation starter, or a contribution.

Before You Write, Understand Your Platform

In nonfiction publishing, you will hear the word “platform” a lot. Your platform is essentially your existing ability to reach the people who might buy and read your book. It is not limited to social media followers. It can include a LinkedIn audience, newsletter subscribers, podcast listeners, speaking engagements, association leadership, clients, professional networks, media appearances, prior publications, courses, or a recognized position in a particular industry.

Publishers care about platform because they are making a commercial bet. A terrific manuscript helps, but a publisher also wants to know who is going to buy it and how those readers will hear about it. If you already speak to 5,000 people at conferences each year, have 30,000 engaged followers, publish regularly in respected outlets, or lead an organization whose members are the natural audience for your book, you have reduced some of the publisher’s risk.

There is no magic follower number. Ten thousand people who actually care about your subject may be more valuable than 100,000 people who followed you for something unrelated. Engagement, credibility, access, and fit matter. The better question is not “How many followers do I need?” It is “Can I identify a meaningful audience that knows me, trusts me, and has a reason to care about this book?”

If your platform is small, start building it before the book comes out. Write articles. Speak. Post useful material. Appear on podcasts. Start a newsletter. Participate in the organizations that serve your intended readers. Do it because you have something to contribute, not because you are collecting human beings for a future sales funnel. A real platform is built on trust.

Traditional Publishing: What You Are Really Choosing

Traditional publishing generally means a publishing house acquires your book, pays for the publishing process, and handles editing, design, production, distribution, and at least some marketing. Depending on the deal, you may receive an advance against royalties and then royalties if sales exceed the advance.

The obvious advantages are credibility, professional infrastructure, broader distribution, and a team that knows how to turn a manuscript into a finished book. A recognized publisher can make it easier to get into bookstores, secure media attention, and place the book in channels an individual author can’t reach.

The tradeoffs are control, speed, and economics. Traditional publishing moves slowly. You may have less control over the title, cover, length, release date, pricing, and sometimes the substance. The publisher owns the commercial process. Your royalty on each copy will generally be much smaller than what you could retain through self-publishing.

And getting a traditional deal is not simply a matter of finishing a manuscript and emailing it to a publisher. For many nonfiction projects, the real first product is the book proposal.

The Literary Agent and the Book Proposal

Many major publishers do not want unsolicited submissions. They want literary agents to bring projects to them. An agent understands which editors are acquiring which types of books, how to position a project, how to negotiate a publishing agreement, and how to protect the author’s interests.

For a nonfiction book, you often approach agents with a proposal rather than a completed manuscript. A strong proposal typically explains the idea, the audience, why the book matters now, why you are the person to write it, competing or comparable books, your platform, your marketing reach, a chapter outline, and sample chapters.

That proposal forces you to answer questions you should answer anyway. Who is this for? What problem does it solve? Why will someone buy it instead of the 50 books already addressing the same general subject? What is your distinct point of view? How will readers find you?

Finding an agent requires research. Look for agents who represent nonfiction in your category. Review books similar to yours and see who represented the authors. Read agency submission guidelines and follow them. A generic blast to hundreds of agents is easy to send and easy to ignore. A thoughtful query showing that you understand an agent’s list is more work, but publishing has never been a business in which avoiding the work is a competitive advantage.

Rejection is part of the process. A rejection does not necessarily mean the book is bad. It can mean the timing is wrong, the category is crowded, the platform isn’t large enough, the agent doesn’t know the right editor for it, or the project doesn’t fit that agent’s list.

Self-Publishing Is Publishing — But You Become the Publisher

Self-publishing has changed dramatically. You can now produce a professional book, sell print and electronic editions, and reach readers around the world without persuading a traditional publishing house to acquire the project.

The advantages are significant. You control the content, title, cover, price, timing, updates, and marketing. You can move much faster. Your per-copy economics can be better. If your book serves a narrow professional audience that you already know how to reach, self-publishing can make enormous sense.

But “self-publishing” should not mean “I did everything myself.” Traditional publishers employ editors, copy editors, proofreaders, designers, production specialists, and marketers for a reason. If you self-publish, you are taking responsibility for assembling those functions. Hire a good editor. Have someone proofread the final text. Invest in a professional cover. Make the interior look like a real book. A reader should not be able to identify your publishing model from the quality of the finished product.

The biggest danger in self-publishing is that no gatekeeper will tell you the book isn’t ready. Freedom is useful. So is friction. Create your own quality-control process.

Which Path Should You Choose?

Your goal should drive the decision. If your dream is national bookstore distribution, major media, and the validation and infrastructure of an established publishing house, pursuing an agent and traditional publisher may be worth the time and rejection that come with it.

If your goal is to get a highly specialized book into the hands of clients, colleagues, conference attendees, students, or members of your profession, self-publishing may be faster and more rational. If you already have direct access to the people most likely to read the book, you may not need a publisher to build a bridge you already possess.

Independent and hybrid publishers also occupy territory between the two models. The arrangements vary widely. Some provide valuable editorial and production services. Others are essentially expensive service packages wrapped in the language of traditional publishing. Read the agreement. Understand who pays whom, who owns the rights, what services are actually included, how distribution works, and what happens if you want your rights back.

Do not choose a publishing model because one sounds more prestigious at a cocktail party. Choose the one that best serves the book and the reason you wrote it.

Write the Book Only You Can Write

The market doesn’t need another generic book that anyone could have written. Your advantage is your experience, your point of view, your stories, your mistakes, your observations, and the conclusions you reached after doing the work.

That does not mean the book has to be about you. Usually it should not be. The reader should remain at the center. Your experiences matter only insofar as they help the reader understand something, avoid something, accomplish something, or see something differently.

Before writing 60,000 words, be able to explain the book in a few sentences. Identify the reader. Identify what that reader wants or needs. Identify what will be different after the reader finishes the book. Then build the chapters around that promise.

And finish it. The publishing world is filled with people who are “working on a book.” At some point, you have to stop talking about being an author and sit down long enough, often enough, to become one.

The Book Is the Beginning, Not the End

Whether you traditionally publish or self-publish, you will probably have to promote the book. Publishers can help, but authors should not assume that a publishing contract comes with an unlimited marketing machine. You may still write articles, appear on podcasts, speak at conferences, post online, contact organizations, and introduce the book to the communities most likely to benefit from it.

That is another reason your motivation matters. If you wrote the book because you care about the subject, promotion feels less like asking strangers to buy something and more like continuing the conversation that caused you to write it.

A book can travel farther than you do. It can reach someone you will never meet. It can sit on a shelf for years and become useful at exactly the moment someone needs it. It can establish an idea, preserve what you learned, and create opportunities you could not predict when you wrote the first page.

Very few of us are going to get rich writing nonfiction books. That is fine. Money is only one measure of return. If you have something worth saying, know who you want to say it to, and are willing to do the work to say it well, publishing a book can still be one of the most worthwhile professional projects you undertake.

Frank Ramos is a partner at Goldberg Segalla in Miami, where he practices commercial litigation, products, and catastrophic personal injury. You can follow him on LinkedIn, where he has about 80,000 followers.
